mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (below 0.1%) signals accommodative monetary policy that reduces equity discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through lower cost of capital for corporate cash flows.
failure_condition: Average 20-day SPX return is negative in periods with FEDFUNDS < 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate above 5.0% signals economic distress and reduced consumer spending power, lowering corporate earnings expectations and generating negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and real personal consumption expenditures indicate broad-based consumer demand weakness, reducing corporate revenue growth expectations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline.

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL above 3.0% annualized inflation signals imminent monetary tightening, increasing equity discount rates and producing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL annualized inflation exceeds 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 100 (2017=100) indicates manufacturing contraction and economic slowdown, lowering corporate profit expectations and generating negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is below 100.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts below 500.0 thousand units indicate weak residential demand and broader economic weakness, reducing corporate revenue growth expectations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when HOUST < 500.0.

mechanism_narrative: A regime of high unemployment (UNRATE > 5.0%) and low job growth (PAYEMS growth < 0.5% monthly) signals labor market deterioration and economic slowdown, producing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
regime_hint: high unemployment and low job growth regime
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 5.0% and PAYEMS growth < 0.5% monthly.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in federal funds rate and CPIAUCSL above 3.0% signals aggressive monetary tightening, compressing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL > 3.0%.
